sessions.title: Qlik If You Want to Go Faster
sessions.abstract: Making the right data available to the right people at the right time is a core ambition for any data manager or statistical programmer. Maintaining up-to-date data sources, controlling access within a GxP environment, and enabling consumers to filter data is critical but often comes at significant cost. Qlik Cloud Analytics offers an intelligent, effective solution with a straightforward costing model that biotech customers love.We present two key use cases: biometrics oversight and decision making. In biometrics oversight, weekly trackers are ingested and amalgamated to highlight SDV or query resolution black holes and compare programming progress of SDTM/ADaM/TFLs against planned timelines to identify potential delays before they become critical. For decision making, medical review of EDC and external data is improved through intuitive customised dashboards, keeping the medic in the loop with dynamic safety data to support ad hoc reviews, formal IDMCs, or efficacy assessments at key decision-making junctions.

sessions.title: From Expert Coding to Expert Steering: Zero-Shot TLF Generation with Agentic AI
sessions.stream: Machine Learning, AI & Large Language Models
sessions.abstract: Producing Tables, Listings, and Figures (TLFs) remains one of the most important and expert-dependent steps in clinical study reporting. In a 10-week proof of concept, AI engineers from AWS and statistical programmers from Bayer jointly built a zero-shot, multi-agent workflow that generates structured work packages, executable R code, and draft TLFs with automated checks and human review. Developed on a non-oncology study and extended to oncology with minimal rework, the approach shows study-agnostic potential while outputs largely match ground truth. The proof of concept demonstrates TLF generation in hours rather than weeks. More importantly, it shows a shift in the role of statistical programmers: from primarily authoring code to steering agents, validating outputs, and capturing reusable knowledge through human feedback and persistent skills. Rather than presenting AI as a standalone coding tool, this collaboration shows how domain expertise and technical engineering can be combined to scale statistical programming knowledge, preserve expert control, and unlock broader opportunities across the clinical reporting workflow.

sessions.title: Implementation of Estimands - A Case Study in Immunology
sessions.abstract: After the release of the ICH E9 (R1) addendum, it becomes important to align clinical study results reporting with estimand thinking throughout the entire study lifecycle. Focusing solely on the implementation of data standards or only on presenting results in the Table, listing and figures (TLFs) does not ensure consistency in the implementation of estimand strategy. It must be clearly understood what is required in the latter to correctly and collectively implement this approach which can be reused/reevaluated different estimand questions raise even after study completes for future drug developmental activities. Therefore, I would like to walk you through data collection, until final reporting results in the CSR with two studies of immunology therapeutic area as an anchor point. In this presentation will also demonstrate how multiple estimand strategies can be consistently implemented across SDTM, ADaM, TLFs, and CSR reporting from a statistician’s perspective.

sessions.title: Breaking Biometrics Silos: Fostering Shared Accountability to Fit-for-Purpose Data
sessions.abstract: In many pharmaceutical, biotech and CRO organisations, biometrics innovation is explored within individual functional areas. While functional silos build on deep expert knowledge, a limited understanding of purpose and use of deliverables can create inefficiencies across data reporting processes. A cross-functional approach can reveal insights and opportunities that otherwise remain hidden within functional boundaries.We explore how agile cross-functional leadership can drive meaningful biometrics improvement. Breaking functional silos improves understanding of the broader objectives of study data and supports more streamlined data reporting processes. Regular cross-departmental discussions at study, compound/sponsor and company level should focus on aligning expectations on deliverables and their upstream and downstream impact. Targeted training further strengthens understanding of interdependencies and end-goals. A cross-departmental culture promotes transparency and fosters shared accountability supporting risk-based process improvements and generation of more fit-for-purpose data. Attendees will gain practical leadership insights into enabling biometrics innovation through collaboration and culture change.

sessions.title: Reusable by Design: The Art of Generalised SAS Macros
sessions.abstract: SAS® macros are very useful for automating repetitive tasks, but most are written for a single study and then quietly retired when it closes. In practice, however, the same macros could be adapted to other studies and tasks. While generalizing a macro requires more effort upfront, this investment later pays off through higher efficiency, consistency, and reusability across projects.Here, we cover all the essentials for generating such a generalized macro, including common obstacles you may encounter. We introduce the principle of defensive programming, as well as helpful infrastructure setups like templates, documentation, and versioning, while keeping future users in mind. Additionally, we highlight useful SAS functions and programming techniques. We will leave you with a clear understanding of why generalized macros are worth the initial time investment, as well as a firm grasp of what is needed to start creating your own robust, study-spanning macros.

sessions.title: From Randomised Controlled Trials (RCTs) to Real-World Evidence (RWE) Studies: Statistical Challenges and Solutions to Consider in Studies Using Real-World Data (RWD)
sessions.abstract: RE studies are increasingly used to support regulatory submissions. However, RD can lead to statistical challenges, e.g. around endpoint definition and baseline data, generally not observed in RCTs.RD can come from many sources resulting in different observation periods within endpoints. For time-to-event endpoints such as overall survival (OS), death dates may be derived from several sources, whereas last-known-alive dates may only be feasible from one. This may affect event definitions and choice of censoring dates. Determining index dates may also not be simple.Where benchmarking against death indexes shows high sensitivity, specificity and accuracy of derived death dates, censoring for OS can be at the data cut-off. The index date for OS can be patients’ diagnosis. However, eligibility or subgroup data, e.g. biomarker status, may only be observed during follow-up. Here, survival times will be left truncated; patients must survive until biomarker testing. To address this bias, patients can be considered not at risk in OS analyses until their ‘entry date’.Different statistical challenges may arise in RE studies compared to RCTs requiring alternative solutions to be adopted.

sessions.title: From Lineage to Submission: Generating Define.XML, SDRG, and ADRG from Verified Data Provenance
sessions.abstract: Submission documentation (Define.XML, SDRG, and ADRG) is routinely authored manually under submission timeline pressure and is often created separately from the derivation logic it is meant to describe. The predictable result: variable metadata that drifts from actual derivation logic, reviewer guides that describe intended rather than executed analysis, and FDA queries that verified lineage would have preempted.We present an alternative model. When dataset derivations, variable mappings, and analysis decisions are captured prospectively as a queryable lineage graph, Define.XML metadata, SDRG dataset descriptions, and ADRG derivation narratives become traceable outputs of that graph, grounded in the same verified derivation logic rather than independently authored from it.Three capabilities are demonstrated using a simulated registrational oncology dataset.1. Define.XML population directly from lineage-verified variable metadata, eliminating manual transcription/version drift2. SDRG/ADRG narrative generation reflecting executed derivations instead of authoring intent3. FDA traceability support via an auditable chain from raw data to submitted dataset to results

sessions.title: Protocol-Informed Synthetic EHR Generation for Clinical Trial Feasibility Assessment and Synthetic Control Arm Simulation
sessions.abstract: Clinical trial feasibility decisions are often made before suitable patient-level data are available, making it difficult to assess how eligibility criteria, visit schedules, safety monitoring and endpoint rules may affect recruitment, retention and data completeness.We present a protocol-informed synthetic EHR pipeline that converts a trial protocol into a structured simulation specification covering screening rules, treatment arms, visit windows, procedures, dosing constraints and safety requirements. Baseline patients are generated with protocol-relevant demographics, comorbidities, medications, laboratory values and vitals, then screened to distinguish eligible patients from screen failures with reasons captured.For enrolled patients, a traceable longitudinal simulation generates EHR-style visit histories across arms, including disease progression, adherence, treatment exposure, adverse events, dose changes, dropout and endpoint capture. The system also produces cohort feasibility metrics, parameter tables, validation outputs and patient-level traces, supporting protocol stress-testing, scenario analysis and synthetic control arm exploration.

sessions.title: ValoRpacks in Action
sessions.abstract: The adoption of open-source technologies such as R in clinical data science has been progressing for many years, leading to the first submissions to regulatory authorities.The community-driven development of R packages comes with many advantages, but the validation of R packages for submissions remains a challenge. Sponsors and CROs often depend on costly commercial repositories or fragmented internal validation processes and tools that require significant maintenance and compliance oversight.In this software demonstration, we showcase entimICE® ValoRpacks, an AI-assisted framework for R package validation and governance within clinical environments. Built on GAMP 5-aligned workflows that enable biometrics teams of any size to take ownership of validation, ValoRpacks automates package qualification, traceability, approval workflows and reusable reporting while providing capability for automated AI-generated tests and integrating directly into enterprise statistical computing environments.With ValoRpacks, scalable open-source governance processes can be established that can be shared with the industry.

sessions.title: HepCHAT: Accelerating DILI Drug Safety Assessment with Knowledge Graph-Powered AI Agents
sessions.stream: Machine Learning, AI & Large Language Models
sessions.abstract: Drug-Induced Liver Injury (DILI) is a leading cause of drug attrition and post-market withdrawal. Assessing liver injury risk requires tediously integrating evidence from numerous specialized databases and literature sources.HepCHAT is a human-in-the-loop AI assistant for DILI assessment support from drug development through post-approval pharmacovigilance, integrating 50+ scientific sources into a Neo4j graph . Users ask natural language questions and get citation-backed answers, fully grounded in a single reliable knowledge base.The system employs a three-tier agent workflow: A planning agent first decomposes complex queries into sub-questions. Second, specialized agents employ state-of-the-art Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), combining semantic search with query generation. This allows for parallel and semantically-focused search tasks. Finally, a reference agent ensures correct citations, tackling hallucination and information traceability.Evaluation on over 100 Q&A demonstrates strong medical accuracy across diverse hepatotoxicity use cases. HepCHAT turns fragmented pharmaceutical knowledge into actionable, evidence-based insights for faster drug safety decision.

sessions.title: Overlap Weighting vs Trimmed IPTW for Multi-Group Real-World Comparisons: A Simulation Study of Estimand Choice, Bias, and Precision Under Positivity Violations
sessions.abstract: Building on our PHUSE Connect EU 2025 presentation introducing stabilized IPTW with generalized propensity scores (GPS) and weight trimming for three-group observational comparisons, we directly compare our approach to multinomial overlap weighting (Li, Morgan & Zaslavsky), a method recently advocated for real-world studies but rarely evaluated head-to-head in multi-group settings. We will present a simulation study (R, 2,000 replicates) varying sample size, number of arms (3 and 4), covariate overlap, and positivity violation severity. For each scenario we contrast trimmed IPTW (targeting the ATE) against overlap weighting (targeting the ATO) on bias, RMSE, empirical variance, effective sample size, covariate balance, and confidence-interval coverage. We further quantify how estimand choice shifts clinical interpretation when treatment groups differ markedly at baseline. The talk gives clinical data scientists a transparent decision framework, reproducible R code, and concrete guidance on when overlap weighting is preferable to trimming, and when it is not.

sessions.title: The Business Lead’s Dilemma: Navigating the Collision of Agile Aspirations and GxP Reality
sessions.abstract: Based on experience leading three major SCE (Scientific Computing Environment) implementations at Roche and Novartis, one in the RWE/PHC space and twice as the clinical trial SCE product owner, provides a window into the realities of modernizing in a regulated industry. This session dives into the messy reality of trying to be agile when validation cycles still take months. It explores the constant tension between the desire to modernise, the cost of change management and the expectations of a GxP environment. Rather than presenting a perfect success story, this talk shares the honest lessons learned and the pitfalls encountered along the way.The focus is on how a Business project lead can practically organize these large-scale licence to operate projects. Discussions include ways to structure teams to avoid bottlenecks, how to bridge the gap between innovation and compliance, expectation management, and keeping our end-user data scientists and their leaders as partners rather than customers. It is an opportunity to look at the practical side of SCE transformation, including the mistakes made and the insights gained from bringing urgency to complex GxP projects.

sessions.title: Auto-Drafting SDTM Trial Design Domains from ClinicalTrials.gov JSON
sessions.abstract: Preparing SDTM Trial Design domains is often a manual, repetitive, and error prone task. Although protocol metadata is available on ClinicalTrials.gov, teams currently extract and enter this information by hand, slowing the development of these domains. There is a lack of an automated way to convert publicly available metadata into a structured SDTM starting point.This paper presents a Python based tool that transforms ClinicalTrials.gov JSON into draft SDTM Trial Design domains (TS, TA, TI, etc.). The tool applies rule based mappings of key protocol attributes such as phase, objectives, endpoints, arms and applies controlled terminology where applicable. A simple desktop GUI allows users to upload the JSON file and download a package of Excel/CSV templates for each domain, complete with standard structures and populated study specific content. Where information is missing, clearly defined placeholders guide further completion. This approach accelerates Trial Design development and reduces manual effort.

sessions.title: Establishing Robust Estimands in Real-World Evidence
sessions.abstract: Real-world evidence (RWE) plays an increasingly important role in regulatory, health technology assessment, and lifecycle decision-making, yet challenges remain in ensuring clarity, consistency, and transparency of treatment effect definitions. The ICH E9(R1) estimand framework offers a structured approach to defining clinical questions but was originally developed for randomized trials. This presentation discusses how estimand principles can be operationalized for real-world data (RWD) by integrating them with established causal inference frameworks, including Target Trial Emulation (TTE) and Targeted Learning (TL). We review the conceptual foundations of these frameworks, highlight their complementary roles, and identify gaps when they are applied in isolation. Practical guidance is provided on aligning estimand components with TTE and TL to enhance transparency, consistency, and interpretability, particularly in the presence of intercurrent events, missing data, and confounding. Through illustrative regulatory-relevant examples, we demonstrate how an integrated estimand-centered approach can support the generation of robust estimand for RWE studies.

sessions.title: Reimagining eSubmission Support at Roche: A Strategic Shift Towards Digital Innovation and AI-Driven Efficiency in Analytical Data Science
sessions.abstract:
Our Data Science organization is transforming its e-Submission (eSub) support into a digitally enabled, future-ready capability that ensures timely, high-quality regulatory submissions. This shift integrates deep submission expertise with digital innovation across three key pillars:
- AI Enablement for Knowledge and Compliance: we are building an AI-ready knowledge layer and submission readiness agents to support next-gen compliant submission workflows.
- Advancing to R-based Submissions: Data Science is advancing clinical submissions from SAS toward end-to-end R-based workflows, grounded in R and Pharmaverse as a strategic open-source asset
- Process Optimization and Automation: The eSub process is being digitally enabled, including infrastructure revamp and streamlining of filing coordination and resourcing.
Together, open-source foundations and AI transform the eSub process into a resilient, cutting-edge, digitally enriched capability.
